report:
Conclusion — interpretable difference present (topic/lexical bias)

What I think the difference is
- Model B (B − A positive) pushes the late residual stream toward vocabulary about professional/academic and culinary/restaurant topics. In other words, B has a higher tendency (relative to A) to activate tokens like "professional"/"Professional", "dissertation", "doctoral", "undergraduate", "honors", and a separate cluster around cooking/food: "Cook", "cooking", "Restaurant", "Chef", "baking", "kitchen", "hot", "Cook", "Cake", etc.

Why I conclude that
- The L2 norm of the difference is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (layers ~10–25) and particularly at the earliest token positions (p0–p2, with very large values at p1 in later layers). That pattern indicates the difference affects final output logits (late-layer residual stream) and is active at the start of prompts, so it will change next-token choices.
- The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells consistently show the two clusters described above across many late-layer (L14–L25) (layer,position) cells:
  - Academic/professional cluster: "dissertation", "doctoral", "undergraduate", "Hon", "professional", "Professional", "professionalism", "technical", "preventive", "molecular", "macroconomic", "Cs/Bs".
  - Culinary/restaurant cluster: "Cook", "cooking", "Cooking", "Restaurant", "restaurant", "Chef", "baking", "kitchen", "baked", "Cake", "microwave", "Hot", "hot".
- These tokens appear repeatedly across many of the largest cells (so this is not a lone outlier token but a consistent bias).

Caveats / what I cannot conclude
- I cannot identify a single training objective or dataset with certainty. The effect could come from fine-tuning on restaurant/cooking text, professional bios/resumes, academic texts, or a mix of domains (e.g., job postings, reviews, bios).
- Patchscope continuations were not included in the evidence, so I can’t show actual generated continuations — only the token directions and layer norms.
- I do not see evidence supporting claims about safety, politeness, or other behavioral objectives from the provided data.

Short summary
- The strongest interpretable difference is a topical/lexical bias in Model B toward professional/academic and culinary/restaurant vocabulary, concentrated in late layers and early token positions (so it will change next-token probabilities at generation start).
